findings.namedBuyers: Two verified commercially relevant organizer contacts: Natalie Gonsalves, Marketing & Events Officer, is the first operational route for event logistics and identifying who handles visiting-speaker/delegate accommodation; Akshita Vincent, Director, Strategy & Partnerships, is the senior relationship/partnership route. Role relevance is an inference from their published remits, not evidence either controls hotel contracts. No named housing manager or accommodation procurement signatory was identified. Route an inquiry to Natalie via the published PRiME inbox rather than inventing a personal address.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced upcoming 8th edition: Thursday, February 18, 2027, 08:00–18:00, Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College St, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This is the activity date, not an article publication date, and falls within the requested horizon. The organizer page and organizer-hosted registration listing agree. No later U of T PRiME symposium edition/date was found announced through June 2028; do not substitute the unrelated electrochemistry PRiME 2028 conference.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: pursue only a conditional short-stay visiting-speaker/VIP or non-local delegate lodging opportunity. The one-day academic symposium does not establish relocation or extended-stay demand. Historical attendance was nearly 200 in 2026 and around 250 in 2025, but attendance is not sleeping-room demand; 2027 attendance and non-local share are unpublished. A subset could use a 157-room city hotel, but there is no evidence supporting a 15–109-room block or an exclusive hotel buyout. The Harbourfront property is away from the College Street venue; do not sell its MTCC walkability as event adjacency. City-hotel lodging is more relevant than resort positioning; the main meeting and included hospitality are already programmed at the campus. Do not offer an unverified hotel catering solution.
findings.venueCommitments: The organizer explicitly publishes: “Location: Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College St, Toronto, ON M5G 0C6.” This is a confirmed published event venue, not proof of an executed venue contract. The university venue describes itself as downtown Toronto, Discovery District, adjacent to St. George campus: Toronto proper and within the broader downtown territory, but not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. It is an innovation/university venue, not a competing hotel. Event room/floor and contractual terms are unpublished.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified selected timeline: 4th edition October 25, 2022 at MaRS Discovery Centre Auditorium; 5th February 20, 2024 at Myhal Centre for Engineering Innovation & Entrepreneurship Auditorium, 55 St. George Street; 6th February 21, 2025 at Leslie Dan Faculty of Pharmacy, 144 College Street; 7th February 20, 2026 at B150 Lecture Hall & Atrium at that same faculty; upcoming 8th February 18, 2027 moves to Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College Street. Evidence supports local academic/innovation venue changes, not destination rotation or a hotel-hosting pattern. Annual branding and 2024–2027 consecutive editions are verified; no 2023 edition is established by the researched sources.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. Neither the official 2027 event page nor its registration listing publishes an accommodation section, official housing bureau, host hotel, room block, hotel booking code, room allotment, or open hotel RFP. Every edition-specific hotel identified: none. This absence does not establish that sourcing is open or that no private arrangements exist. The published contact route is: “For sponsorship and donation opportunities, please contact prime.initiative@utoronto.ca”; it is an organizer routing contact, not a published housing desk. The event page also states: “Symposium ticket fee includes breakfast, lunch, snacks, beverages, and evening reception.” No source quotation establishing a lodging mechanism is available.
findings.organizationStructure: PRiME is the University of Toronto’s next-generation precision medicine institutional strategic initiative, established in 2019; it is not evidenced as a standalone trade association, corporate event company, PCO or DMC. PRiME/U of T is the event organizer; Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus is the venue; Luma is the published registration platform, not an identified housing buyer. No external PCO/DMC is named in the reviewed event materials.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent hotel, exclusive housing arrangement, sold-out allocation, compression, or overflow need is publicly evidenced. The actual limitation is the confirmed non-hotel meeting venue and included breakfast/lunch/reception, not a named lodging competitor. The organizer’s university/hospital research audience does not establish how many need overnight stays. Inference: location nearer College Street could influence hotel choice, but no competing hotel commitment or rate comparison is verified. With the supplied approximately 240-theatre ballroom limit, historical attendance around 250 also makes a full future symposium relocation uncertain even before poster/catering requirements.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Natalie Gonsalves via prime.initiative@utoronto.ca, referencing the February 18, 2027 symposium at 108 College Street. Ask who books and pays for visiting speakers, whether any lodging contracts or university arrangements already apply, anticipated non-local attendees, arrival/departure nights and actual peak rooms. Request an introduction to the authorized accommodation buyer; involve Akshita Vincent for a broader recurring relationship only if relevant. Offer a tailored short-stay lodging proposal after need, procurement route and availability are confirmed, without a speculative block or catering promise. If 2027 lodging is already handled, ask for the next accommodation review window; do not invent a 2028 edition date.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: As of the supplied November 16, 2026 research date, February 18, 2027 is upcoming and public registration is offered. Commercial accessibility is unconfirmed: the symposium venue is selected, but neither an open hotel procurement process nor a closed/exclusive lodging commitment is published. Seek permission to discuss accommodation needs; do not label the event an open RFP, verified overflow, or displacement opportunity.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: build a recurring organizer relationship for visiting-speaker and non-local delegate lodging, independent of the campus symposium venue. Consecutive 2024–2027 editions support recurrence, not a confirmed 2028 date, room requirement or venue change. Prioritize accommodation capture over displacing the main meeting. Future off-site small meetings would require explicit organizer demand and confirmation of the hotel’s operational capabilities.
